messages:
incident-bot: [Pager] Elevated tail latency and truncated streams on /v1/chat/stream. Paging oncall. Warroom created: https://meet.redwood.example/warrooms/xyz789

jules: Oncall here, joining warroom. Anyone want to own comms & status updates? I can handle triage.

katie: I'll take customer comms and status page. Posting quick draft in a sec.

raj: Jumping in. My initial glance shows spike in goroutine queues on the runtime hosts in us-east-2. Could be a memory pressure causing stream handler stalls.

devops-bot: Deploy detected: canary/stream-processor rolled at 2026-03-15T14:05:00Z by ci-cd. No immediate failures in deploy logs.

jules: Noted. Priorities: 1) confirm whether deploy correlates 2) throttle non-critical inference jobs 3) add temporary routing exception to avoid overloaded nodes. I'll run a quick healthcheck script.

leo: Healthcheck output (pasted):
```
$ ./ops/healthcheck --hosts=runtime-us-east-2
host-a: stream_handler loop delay=320ms mem=78% fd=120/1024
host-b: stream_handler delay=15ms mem=45% fd=90/1024
host-c: stream_handler delay=410ms mem=92% fd=200/1024
```

raj: host-c looks saturated. Taking it out of rotation: `/infra/pool/drain --pool=runtime-us-east-2 --host=host-c` (doing now).

incident-bot: ACTION: host-c removed from rotation (action_id: a-3345). Queues draining.

katie: Status page draft:
```
Status: Partial service degradation (chat streaming)
Start: 2026-03-15T14:05:00Z
Scope: Streaming chat endpoint (/v1/chat/stream)
Impact: Some customers in US-East may see stalled or truncated streaming responses. Non-streaming requests unaffected.
Mitigation: We are removing affected host(s) from rotation and investigating memory pressure. Next update in 15 minutes.
```

jules: Good. Also adding a note to ops: avoid large batch offline jobs hitting same pool. Raj, can you check if any background indexing tasks coincided?

raj: Confirmed: a nightly embedding job kicked at 14:02 UTC and targeted runtime-us-east-2 as a fallback. I've paused that job and will update the scheduler rule to avoid runtime pools. Ticket INFRA-4820.

katie: Customer notification draft:
```
Subject: Service degradation affecting chat streaming
Body: Hi 4E9 between ~14:05 UTC we saw interruptions to the chat streaming endpoint for some customers in US-East. We have removed the impacted host from rotation and are investigating root cause. No customer data loss is expected. We will follow up with a post-incident summary.
```

leo: After draining host-c, stream latency trending back to baseline. Monitoring shows 95th percentile dropping from 1.2s to 120ms.

incident-bot: METRICS: 95p latency for streaming peaked at 1.2s at 14:07 UTC; now 0.12s. Error rate stable at 0.4%.

oncall: All pages acknowledged; remaining actions: monitor for 30m, run postmortem, and update runbook with embedding job scheduling isolation. I'll stay on watch.

jules: I'll write the incident timeline and assign the postmortem to raj for root-cause and to leo for mitigation follow-ups. katie will lead customer comms. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

katie: Posting status update and sending targeted emails to affected accounts. Will include request ids if customers reply.

raj: Filing infra follow-up: INFRA-4820, linking to scheduling config and adding a canary rollout for future offload jobs.

incident-bot: STATUS: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2026-03-15-chat-streaming

jules: War room remains open. If no regressions in 30m, we'll close and hand off.
